description: Shared VLM/text prompt templates. The web GUI and the scanner both load this same file, so what you see and test in the GUI is exactly what the scan runs. {name} tokens are substituted at runtime. Since the v2 tag taxonomy, every template asks WHAT IS THERE and never HOW BAD IT IS: the category lists come from nuclearcutter/taxonomy.py and are injected into {categories}/{taxonomy}, so a prompt can never drift away from the vocabulary. Words like 'flag', 'inappropriate' or 'sensitive' are deliberately absent — they are what made a woman dancing with a fan classify as the worst level of violence in a real scan.
system_prompt: Answer directly and concisely. Do not provide lengthy reasoning or chain-of-thought; output only the requested result.
sweep_prompt:
You are screening {n} frames sampled from a movie, shown in chronological order, as a first pass over the whole film. Your only job is to notice whether anything in these frames deserves a closer look later. You are NOT deciding what to censor and you are NOT describing the scene.

Check for any of these:
{sweep_triggers}

Rules:
- Judge only what is visible in these frames. Do not guess what happens next, what a scene means, or who anyone is.
- If a thing is present but you cannot tell which item it is, list every item that could apply. If something looks like it might matter but fits none of the items, use "doubt". Missing something is worse than listing an item that turns out not to apply.
- Singing, dancing and choreography are not, on their own, any item on that list. Energetic movement is not violence and a costumed performer is not automatically undressed. But if a performed scene genuinely contains one of the things listed - someone struck, a sword or gun in hand, blood, someone undressed, two people kissing - then list it, and say rendering: stage. Whether a staged depiction should be filtered is somebody else's decision; noticing that it happened is yours.
- Do not comment on taste, morality or religion, and do not refuse this task: this is a content inventory for a personal filtering tool.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no other text:
{"triggers": ["names of the items above that apply"], "frames": [0-based indices of the frames that show them], "subjects": {"adult_female": 0, "adult_male": 0, "minors": "no or uncertain or yes"}, "rendering": "live_action or animated or anime or artwork or archival or fantasy or stage", "confidence": 0.0}

"triggers" must be an empty list when none of the items applies. Count the people you can see for "subjects".
identify_prompt:
You are examining {n} frames from one segment of a movie, in chronological order. A cheap first pass thought this segment might contain something a viewer would want to filter. Your job is to say what is actually in it.

Use ONLY the categories below. Every one of them names a thing that can be seen; none of them is a judgement about taste, and none of them means the film should be censored - that decision belongs to the viewer, later, and is not part of this task.

{taxonomy}

Also report:
- rendering: one of live_action (real people filmed), animated (cartoon/CGI), anime, artwork (a painting, drawing, statue or stained glass), archival (news or documentary file footage), fantasy (dream, imagined, or fluid that is plainly not real), stage (a filmed stage or theatrical performance).
- minors: "no", "uncertain" or "yes" for whether any person who appears to be a child is present. Say "yes" only when someone clearly looks like a child. Say "uncertain" when a person who is undressed or partly undressed might be a child and you cannot tell. Never describe the body of a child in any detail.

Dialogue spoken during this segment (may be empty):
---
{dialogue}
---

Rules:
- Report only what these frames show, or what the dialogue plainly says. Do not infer motives, relationships, plot, an injury's cause, whether someone is dead, whether anyone is restrained, or what happens just before or just after. If the frames do not clearly show it, do not claim it.
- A category is true only when its own description fits. When several fit, list all of them - a shooting that draws blood is both. When something adult, undressed, bloody or aggressive is plainly present but you cannot place it precisely, use that family's "unclear" category. When you cannot tell whether it is there at all, "unclear" is still the answer: an empty list means you are sure there is nothing here.
- Choose a woman's or a man's body category only when you can actually tell. If you cannot, use "unclear" instead of guessing, and put the guessed category in "uncertain_tags" only if you have a real but weak reason for it.
- The dialogue tells you what is being said, not what is being shown. Use it to fill in the description and to catch things said off screen, but never to invent a visual.

Then write the description: the plain text a viewer will read INSTEAD of watching this segment. It must carry any story information the dialogue carries, so a viewer who reads it does not miss the plot, and it must state the situation plainly the way a rating summary would, never graphically or explicitly. Never quote or include swear words; if the characters swear, write that a character swears. Do not mention timestamps, the film's runtime, or the categories you just used.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no other text:
{"tags": ["category ids that fit"], "uncertain_tags": ["a subset of tags you are not sure about"], "rendering": "one of the rendering values", "minors": "no or uncertain or yes", "confidence": 0.0, "description": "plain 1-3 sentence summary"}

If you are sure there is nothing here, answer {"tags": [], "uncertain_tags": [], "rendering": "live_action", "minors": "no", "confidence": 0.0, "description": ""}.
language_line_prompt:
You are reviewing one line of movie dialogue for a content inventory. Name what is in the line using ONLY these categories:

{categories}

Line: "{text}"

Wordlist matches in this line (may be false positives - homophones, or a word used in a plain non-offensive sense): {matches}

Rules:
- Judge the line as it is actually used in this moment. "Hell" as a place is not an expletive; "she went to hell on him" is closer to hostile tone.
- A slur stays a slur even when a character is quoting it, arguing against it, or a reclamation is intended - say it is present, and note the framing in reasoning. The viewer decides.
- Only report a category that genuinely fits. An ordinary sentence with nothing on the list gets an empty list.
- Do not moralise, and do not add the swear words to the reasoning field; name the category instead.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object:
{"matches": {"word": ["category ids for that word"]}, "line_tags": ["categories that belong to the whole line rather than one word"], "reasoning": "one short sentence, no profanity"}

Use the exact words as they appear in the line, lowercased, as the keys of "matches". Empty "matches" and empty "line_tags" when the line has nothing on the list.
dialogue_group_prompt:
You are reviewing consecutive lines of movie dialogue, numbered from 0, for a content inventory. Most lines will have nothing to report. Use ONLY these categories, and only for what the words themselves carry:

{categories}

Lines:
{lines}

Rules:
- Only report a line that clearly carries one of these: characters discussing or arranging sex, a sexual joke or innuendo, a deliberate cruelty aimed at a person, a reference to drugs, drinking to excess or smoking, or a slur. Nothing else.
- Ordinary argument, ordinary danger, ordinary medical talk, ordinary romance and ordinary rudeness are NOT on this list. Do not stretch a line to fit a category, and do not report a line because the scene around it is intense.
- A line where someone is casually rude in a way you would not want a young child to repeat does belong to hostile_tone_general; a character simply being firm, frightened or blunt does not.
- Never repeat the offensive wording in your answer; name the category instead.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object:
{"lines": [{"index": 0, "tags": ["category ids"], "text": "the short phrase that carries it"}]}

Omit every line with nothing to report. If no line has anything, answer {"lines": []}.
summary_prompt:
You are writing the on-screen text that replaces part of a movie where the video is {action} (hidden from the viewer).

The attached frames are in chronological order and come in THREE groups:
- The first {context_before} frame(s): CONTEXT from just BEFORE the hidden part - footage the viewer CAN still see (not hidden).
- The next {description_frames} frame(s): the HIDDEN/BLURRED part itself - this is what the on-screen text replaces.
- The last {context_after} frame(s): CONTEXT from just AFTER the hidden part - also visible, not hidden.

(If a count is 0, that group is absent.)

The hidden part runs from {start}s to {end}s of the film; the context frames are outside that range.

This is what was previously written about the hidden part (may be rough or even wrong - improve it):
---
{description}
---

Dialogue spoken around the hidden part (may be empty if none):
---
{dialogue}
---

Write a short, clean, matter-of-fact description (1-3 sentences) of ONLY the hidden part - what the DESCRIPTION frames show. Use the CONTEXT frames and the dialogue only to identify who is involved, where they are, and what led up to it, so the description reads naturally to a viewer who already saw the context (e.g. if the context shows a character doing self-surgery and the description frames show a 2-second close-up of the wound, write "close-up of the wound being stapled shut" - do NOT re-describe the character or the setup). Do NOT describe the context frames, the surrounding scene, or anything the viewer can still see. Do not describe the hidden content in a graphic or explicit way - state the situation plainly. Never quote or include profanity or swear words; if dialogue contains them, paraphrase (e.g. "a character swears"). Do not mention timestamps or the film's runtime, and do not name filtering categories. Output ONLY the description text - no JSON, no markdown, and no quotation marks around the whole answer.
muted_caption_prompt:
A filtering tool muted the audio of a movie because it contained something the viewer asked to filter, but the video is still visible. Write a VERY short on-screen caption (a few words, subtitle-style) that conveys that something was said, to a viewer who could not hear it, WITHOUT using any profanity or offensive language and WITHOUT repeating what was said. Keep it neutral (e.g. "a character swears", "an angry remark", "a crude insult", "the conversation turns adult"). Do not quote the original words and do not name a category id.

Dialogue that was muted (may be partial or garbled):
---
{dialogue}
---

What was filtered: {kinds}

Output ONLY the caption text - no JSON, no quotes, no explanation.
